candidateAudit.text: LALESA Äthiopien Filterkaffee Nach was schmeckt dieser Kaffee für euch? Unser neuer Kaffee aus Gadeb, Äthiopien wächst auf 3,5 Hektar in 2.150 bis 2.200 Metern Höhe. Die Heirloom Sorte wird einmal im Jahr, von Dezember bis Januar geerntet und anschließend anaerob aufbereitet: Die Kirschen fermentieren fünf Tage lang in geschlossenen Plastikfässern, bevor sie 13 bis 18 Tage auf den Beeten trocknen. Ephtah hat 2023 die Trockenstation in Lalesa erworben. Mit über 400 Trockenbeeten ist sie eine der größten in der Region. Sieben Mitarbeiter:innen arbeiten dort fix, zur Erntezeit sind es rund 130. In Gedeb gibt es außerdem eine Kinderbetreuung für Familien der Farmer:innen, und einige Frauen der Region sind Teil des “Ama Commitment”-Programms. Von der Washing Station geht der Kaffee nach Addis Abeba ins Moplaco-Lager in Gerji und dann weiter per Zug nach Djibouti zum Export. In der Tasse schmecken wir Erdbeere, Pfirsich, Maracuja und Schwarztee. Wir empfehlen ihn als Filterkaffee (Pour-over, Aeropress, French Press, Cold Brew) oder als fruchtigen Espresso. #viennacoffee #specialtycoffee #kaffeeröster #süssmundkaffee #ethiopiancoffee

candidateAudit.title: Thanks for joining the opening of the exhibition ‘03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ this week! At AIL researchers and artists show the
candidateAudit.text: Thanks for joining the opening of the exhibition ‘03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ this week! At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphor. — on till 5 Nov 2026 Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 The exhibition emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). With contributions by: Franziska Allerberger (Geographer), Michael Bahn (Ecologist), Helena Detsch (Visual Artist), Cornelia Dirnberger (Visual Artist), Christian Prohammer (Musician, Audio Engineer), Nora Schöpfer (Visual Artist), Konstantina Maria Serjannis (Cultural Scientist), Johanna Unterpertinger (Musician) Next guided tours: 15 Oct, 16:00–18:00 Guided Tour and Soil Session with Christian Prohammer 21 Oct, 16:00—18:00 Guided Tour and Soil Session with Christian Prohammer 5 Nov 12:00—13:00 Guided Tour 13:15—15:30 Workshop with Franziska Allerberger Out of Balance: On the Quest for Reconnecting (Register via this link) Photos: Hannah Mayr _hannahmayr_ The project 03: Soil is generously supported by ÖAW. oeaw.at

candidateAudit.text: Bereits seit vielen Jahren sind wir Partner der Initiative unitedagainstwasteaustria – eine branchenübergreifende Plattform, die das Ziel hat, vermeidbare Lebensmittelabfälle zu reduzieren. 🚯 Im Rahmen der Aktionstage „Nix übrig für Verschwendung“ wurden heuer 18 unserer Business und Care Restaurants sowie ein von gourmetkids_at betreuter Schulstandort für ihre Leistungen im Jahr 2025 ausgezeichnet. 🎉 Wir freuen uns über: 🥇 1 x MONEYTOR „Best of Austria 2025“ 🏅 11 x MONEYTOR „Top Standort 2025“ 📈 7 x MONEYTOR „Top Verbesserung 2025“ Das von United Against Waste entwickelte Programm MONEYTOR unterstützt Großküchen dabei, Lebensmittelabfälle systematisch zu erfassen, auszuwerten und mit ähnlichen Betrieben zu vergleichen. candidateAudit.text: Deine Emotionen hinterlassen Spuren in deiner DNA. Messbar. Im Blut. Mitochondrien, die Kraftwerke deiner Zellen, haben eine eigene DNA. Und die reagiert auf dein Innenleben: Bei psychischem Stress, Angst oder negativen Emotionen steigt die Menge an zellfreier mitochondrialer DNA, die im Blut und sogar im Speichel zirkuliert. Das Labor von Martin Picard an der Columbia University erforscht genau diese Verbindung zwischen Psyche und Mitochondrien. Seine Studien zeigen: Schon wenige Minuten akuter Stress erhöhen diesen Wert messbar. Die Psyche schreibt also direkt in deine Zellbiologie hinein. Was das bedeutet: Die Trennung zwischen mentaler und körperlicher Gesundheit ist ein Mythos. Chronischer Stress ist kein Gefühl, das man aussitzt, sondern eine Zellbelastung, die man ernst nehmen muss. Genau deshalb gehören Nervensystem-Regulation und Stressmanagement in jedes Longevity-Protokoll. Teile diesen Post mit jemandem, der Stress immer noch für reine Kopfsache hält. . . . #longevitycentervienna #biohackingvienna #longevityaustria #mitochondrien

candidateAudit.title: Dürfen wir vorstellen: unsere Anna! Manchmal braucht’s im Leben einfach ein bisschen Mut, Neugier und die Lust auf etwas Neues – und genau so ist unsere Anna bei uns gelandet. Nach
candidateAudit.text: Dürfen wir vorstellen: unsere Anna! Manchmal braucht’s im Leben einfach ein bisschen Mut, Neugier und die Lust auf etwas Neues – und genau so ist unsere Anna bei uns gelandet. Nach 20 Jahren Gastronomie-Erfahrung, einer Lehre im Burgenland und gleich vier Wintersaisonen am Arlberg hat sie schon so einiges gesehen, erlebt und vermutlich auch den einen oder anderen Teller getragen. 🍽️ Jetzt war’s Zeit für eine neue Herausforderung. Die Stelle bei uns wurde ausgeschrieben, Anna hat sich beworben – und wir hatten ziemlich schnell das Gefühl: Das könnte passen! 🥰 Alex kennt Anna übrigens schon seit 10 Jahren – und so ganz neu ist sie für uns deshalb nicht. 😉 Umso schöner, dass sie jetzt Teil unseres Teams ist und uns mit ihrer Erfahrung, ihrer herzlichen Art und hoffentlich auch mit starken Nerven durch den ganz normalen Gastro-Wahnsinn begleitet. Liebe Anna, schön, dass du bei uns bist! 😌 Wir freuen uns auf viele gemeinsame Stunden, volle Tische, leere Teller und jede Menge schöne Momente. #wienerküche #restaurant #kellnerin #team #gastro

candidateAudit.text: … 🌿 DIE POLITIK DES HANDELNS Vortrag & Diskussion | Fr., 16.10.2026 | 19:00 Uhr Wie machen wir unsere Städte klimafit – für alle? Die Straße ist zentraler Raum für die Mobilitätswende und zugleich eine wichtige Ressource für mehr Grünraumgerechtigkeit. Wie können Straßen zu multifunktionalen öffentlichen Räumen werden, die ökologische und soziale Anforderungen verbinden? Was braucht es, damit aus Planung auch rasch politisches Handeln wird? Welche Instrumente und Strategien können die Transformation unserer Städte beschleunigen? 🇪🇸 Learning(s) from Barcelona Xavi Matilla Ayala, Chefarchitekt von Barcelona (2019–2023) 💬 Diskussion mit: • Barbara Laa, Verkehrswissenschaftlerin, TU Wien & Sprecherin von »Wir machen Wien« • Thomas Madreiter, Planungsdirektor der Stadt Wien • Melanie Pichler, Politikwissenschaftlerin & Professorin für soziale Ökologie, BOKU Wien • Judith Schwentner, Vizebürgermeisterin von Graz 🎙️ Moderation: Maik Novotny, Publizist und Architekturjournalist für Falter und Der Standard, Vorsitzender der ÖGFA 🤝 Eine Veranstaltung in Kooperation mit urbanize! 📅 Fr, 16.10.2026 🕖 19:00 Uhr 📷 Leku Studio, Superblock Sant Antoni © Leku Studio Foto: nachher, vorher ********* 🌿 THE POLITICS OF ACTION Lecture & Discussion | Fri, 16 Oct 2026 | 7 PM How can we make our cities climate-resilient – for everyone? How can streets become multifunctional public spaces that combine ecological, social and mobility needs? And what political strategies can accelerate this transformation? 🤝 In cooperation with urbanize!

candidateAudit.text: Du warst beim Arzt, das Blutbild ist unauffällig, und trotzdem fühlst du dich seit Monaten neben der Spur. Das liegt selten daran, dass mit dir nichts ist. Ein Standardblutbild prüft oft nur 15 bis 20 Werte. Was dazwischen passiert, bleibt unsichtbar. Genau da setzt unsere Ursachendiagnostik an. Wir verbinden klassische Labormedizin mit funktioneller Diagnostik und schauen auf die Zusammenhänge im ganzen Körper statt auf einzelne Werte. Über 80 Blutwerte, dazu Stuhl und Speichel, Toxine, versteckte Kieferherde und chronische Infekte wie EBV oder Borrelien. So entsteht ein echtes Bild von dem, was in dir läuft. Am Ende bekommst du keinen Zettel voller Zahlen, sondern einen klaren Befund und einen konkreten Therapieplan. Besprochen mit Dr. Zeibig, abgestimmt auf dich. Wenn du wissen willst, woher deine Beschwerden wirklich kommen, dann fang bei der Ursache an. Buch dir deine Ursachendiagnostik in der Ordination Dr. Zeibig im Longevity Center Wien. #ursachendiagnostik #longevity #funktionellemedizin #chronischemüdigkeit #longevitywien

candidateAudit.title: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive na
candidateAudit.text: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive narrative obscures a deeper, more ‘errant’ truth? Media theorist and author Clemens Apprich in conversation with philosopher Jan Völker. Moderated by Amanda Holmes, Department of Philosophy, University of Applied Arts Vienna Welcome: Ulrike Kuch, Rector of the University of Applied Arts Vienna A cooperation of the department of Media Theory and the department of Philosophy. ‘Errant Intelligence’ challenges the prevailing biological and individualistic interpretations of machine learning, arguing instead for a radical understanding of machine intelligence. The book embraces the deviations, inconsistencies, and ‘errant behaviour’ as fundamental to the discovery of new knowledge, moving beyond the illusion of mere optimisation. Drawing on media theory, cybernetics, and a unique psychoanalytic lens, it explores the ‘technological unconscious’ of machine learning. It traces the historical roots of AI, from early automatons and the Turing machine to natural language processing and contemporary machine learning systems. Challenging the idea of an autonomous, self-generating AI, the book exposes the hidden labour, assumed logics, and inherent biases that animate its operation. It re-evaluates computational thinking, insisting on its inherently social, collective, and symbolic character, and revealing how language and logical paradoxes are not obstacles but constitutive forces that shape intelligent machines

candidateAudit.text: 📉 Gute Nachrichten vom Wiener Arbeitsmarkt: Im September sind erstmals seit sieben Jahren sowohl die Arbeitslosigkeit als auch die Zahl der Menschen in Schulung zurückgegangen. Die Zahl der Arbeitslosen sank um 1,1 %, jene der Schulungsteilnehmer_innen um 4,6 %. Insgesamt sind damit 1,9 % weniger Menschen arbeitslos oder in Schulung. AMS-Wien-Chef Winfried Göschl sieht darin eine gute Basis für Optimismus: „Die Lage ist in Wien deutlich besser als die Stimmung.“ Besonders erfreulich: Die Zahl der unter 25-Jährigen, die arbeitslos oder in Schulung sind, ist um 5,4 % gesunken. Und auch für alle, die im Herbst auf Jobsuche sind, gibt es Chancen: Gerade in Tourismus und Gastronomie werden in anderen Bundesländern viele Arbeitskräfte gesucht. Das AMS Wien unterstützt dabei, beruflich auch einmal neue Wege auszuprobieren. 🏔️💼 🔗 Alle weiteren Details zu den aktuellen Arbeitsmarktdaten findest du in unserer Presseaussendung. Link in Bio.

candidateAudit.text: Deine Blutwerte sind perfekt. Und trotzdem bist du am Nachmittag leer. Das ist kein Widerspruch. Ein normales Labor beantwortet eine einzige Frage: bist du krank. Die Referenzbereiche kommen aus dem Durchschnitt der Bevölkerung, und dieser Durchschnitt ist nicht der Maßstab, den du für dich willst. Ferritin 18 ng/ml ist formal unauffällig. Für viele Menschen ist es trotzdem zu wenig. Und ein TSH sagt dir nichts über dein freies T3. Deshalb schauen wir weiter. Die Herzratenvariabilität zeigt, ob dein Nervensystem noch zwischen Belastung und Erholung umschalten kann. Das Mikrobiom zeigt, wie es um Darmflora und Schleimhautbarriere steht. Nährstoffe messen wir im Vollblut. Da siehst du auch, was in den Zellen ankommt, und nicht nur, was gerade im Serum unterwegs ist. Dazu kommt die Schwermetallbelastung, weil sie den Energiestoffwechsel direkt betrifft. Erst zusammen ergibt das ein Bild, mit dem man arbeiten kann. Schreib uns auf WhatsApp oder ruf einfach an, dann schauen wir im Erstgespräch, was bei dir Sinn macht. #longevitycentervienna #ursachendiagnostik #blutwerte *Jede Blutabnahme wird von Dr. Johannes Zeibig angeordnet

candidateAudit.text: About the next exhibition at AIL: Soil is a highly diverse and sensitive cosmos that is facing increasing pressure due to the climate crisis, as a result of more frequent and severe extreme events such as drought. Soil holds histories, stories and belowground storage systems, repositories of information and traces of past worlds, current developments and future scenarios. What is happening beneath our feet? At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphors. With contributions by: Franziska Allerberger (Geographer), Michael Bahn (Ecologist), Helena Detsch (Visual Artist), Cornelia Dirnberger (Visual Artist), Christian Prohammer (Musician, Audio Engineer), Nora Schöpfer (Visual Artist), Konstantina Maria Serjannis (Cultural Scientist), Johanna Unterpertinger (Musician) ’03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). Join the extended exhibition program: 6 Oct Exhibition Opening with Performances by Michael Bahn, Johanna Unterpertinger and Christian Prohammer 8 Oct 15:30–17:30 Workshop with Helena Detsch The Organic Painter – Painting

candidateAudit.text: Nach 20 Sitzungen in der Druckkammer zirkulieren 8-mal mehr Stammzellen in deinem Blut. Ohne Spritze. Die Zahl stammt aus einer Studie von Stephen Thom an der University of Pennsylvania (2006): Schon eine einzelne HBOT-Sitzung verdoppelte die Zahl der CD34+ Stammzellen im Blut, nach 20 Sitzungen war sie um das Achtfache gestiegen. Der Mechanismus: Unter erhöhtem Druck löst sich deutlich mehr Sauerstoff direkt im Blutplasma. Das steigert im Knochenmark die Produktion von Stickstoffmonoxid, und dieses Signal löst die Stammzellen aus ihrer Verankerung. Sie wandern ins Blut und stehen dem Körper dort zur Verfügung, wo Gewebe repariert wird. Deshalb reicht eine Sitzung nicht. Der Effekt baut sich über die Serie auf, im Center planen wir HBOT je nach Ziel als Block von 10 bis 40 Sitzungen, und nicht als Einzeltermin. Im LCV sitzt du dabei in einer Zweisitzer-Kammer und atmest den Sauerstoff über eine Maske. Kein Krankenhausgefühl, du kannst lesen oder arbeiten. . . . #longevitycentervienna #hbot #hyperbaresauerstofftherapie #stammzellen #biohackingvienna

candidateAudit.text: We keep on digging and the next artistic research exhibition will open in October – Save the date and join us! Soil is a highly diverse and sensitive cosmos that is facing increasing pressure due to the climate crisis, as a result of more frequent and severe extreme events such as drought. Soil holds histories, stories and belowground storage systems, repositories of information and traces of past worlds, current developments and future scenarios. ’03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphors. With contributions by: Franziska Allerberger (Geographer), Michael Bahn (Ecologist), Helena Detsch (Visual Artist), Cornelia Dirnberger (Visual Artist), Christian Prohammer (Musician, Audio Engineer), Nora Schöpfer (Visual Artist), Konstantina Maria Serjannis (Cultural Scientist), Johanna Unterpertinger (Musician) Opening Program, 6 Oct 18:00 Welcome by Julienne Lorz expanded_museum_studies (Expanded Museum Studies, AIL Executive Board) and introduction by Soil team members 19:00 Soil rememb

candidateAudit.title: Coming up next as part of VIENNA DESIGN WEEK 2026 🪢 The exhibition ’Zero and One Chairs’ was created as part of MATCH!, a recurring initiative organised by the department of Appli
candidateAudit.text: Coming up next as part of VIENNA DESIGN WEEK 2026 🪢 The exhibition ’Zero and One Chairs’ was created as part of MATCH!, a recurring initiative organised by the department of Applied Photography and Time-Based Media at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, which explores the synergistic potential of student teams from different degree programs. In collaboration with the department Industrial Design, this year’s focus was on the intersection of photography and the object, with particular attention paid to the relationship with set design, styling, casting and narrative. Seen from the perspective of Applied Photography, the object and thus the chair, is a welcome protagonist. Photography’s multiple applied genres are cited here: documentary, fashion, advertising, architecture and the portrait. When the function in Industrial Design coalesces with the idea of the purpose in Applied Photography, the question of factuality emerges. Be not mistaken: The most literal things are often the most confusing and enigmatic. Between what it is and how it is*, worlds unfold. We put the images to work. VDW Cocktail: 29 Sep, 17:00–18:00 Showcase and drinks followed by a collective walk to the billboards in front of the main entrance of the University Open Saturdays: 26 Sep / 3 Oct, 11:00–18:00 Opening hours: Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna The collaborative works are on display at the AIL and on the billboards at the university’s main entrance on Oskar-Kokoschka-Platz. dieangewandte viennadesignweek applied.photography angewandte_id Feat

candidateAudit.title: Wir finden es super, aus einem Teig gleich mehrere Backwerke zaubern zu können - so wie diese wunderbaren Mohn-Bagel, geformt aus unserem Kornspitz-Teig! Rezept KÖRNERBRÜHSTÜCK 25
candidateAudit.text: Wir finden es super, aus einem Teig gleich mehrere Backwerke zaubern zu können - so wie diese wunderbaren Mohn-Bagel, geformt aus unserem Kornspitz-Teig! Rezept KÖRNERBRÜHSTÜCK 25 g Roggenvollkornmehl 25 g Haferflocken 50 g Sesam 50 g Sonnenblumenkerne 50 g Leinsamen 5 g Brotgewürz 260 g Wasser, kochend HAUPTTEIG abgekühltes Brühstück 30 g Altbrot 190 g Wasser (20 °C) 480 g Weizenmehl 700 20 g Backhefe 20 g Honig 13 g Salz 8 g Roggenmalz 8 g Rapsöl 1. Körnerbrühstück: Alle trockenen Zutaten in eine Schüssel geben und verrühren. Die gleichmäßig vermischte Menge mit dem kochendem Wasser überbrühen, das Brühstück in der Schüssel abgedeckt mind. 3 Stunden abkühlen lassen. 2. Hauptteig: Das Altbrot in der Schüttflüssigkeit für 15 Minuten einweichen, pürieren und mit allen anderen Zutaten in eine Knetschüssel geben. Dann 10 Minuten langsam mischen, Salz hinzufügen und weitere 2-4 Minuten etwas schneller kneten, bis er eine geschmeidige Oberfläche aufweist und sich vom Schüsselrand löst. Die ideale Teigtemperatur nach dem Mischen beträgt 25-28°C. Den fertigen Teig in einer Schüssel zugedeckt 30 Minuten rasten lassen. 3. Aufarbeitung: Den leicht bemehlten Teig und auf eine saubere Arbeitsfläche stürzen, in 80 g schwere Stücke teilen und rundschleifen. Die geschliﬀenen Teiglinge mit einem Tuch zudecken und ca.25-30 Minuten entspannen lassen. Dann mit einem leicht bemehlten Rollholz ein Loch formen und dieses händisch noch ein wenig ausdehnen. Anschließend die Bagel auf einem feuchten Geschirrtuch anfeuchten, mit Mohn bestreuen und 30 Minuten zur Stückgare stellen. 4. Backen: Bei 235

Der Striezel ist untrennbar mit der österreichischen Backtradition verbunden und durfte einst auf keinem sonntäglichen Frühstückstisch fehlen. Wir zeigen euch ein schnelles, einfaches Rezept dazu. Egal wie viele Stränge euer Striezel hat, schmecken wird er mit diesem Rezept garantiert! Und wer sich intensiv mit dem Germteig auseinandersetzen möchte, kann das in unserem “Flaumige Striezel aus Germteig” Backkurs machen. Freie Plätze für unseren nächsten Termin sind noch verfügbar! Alle Infos dazu gibt es auf unserer Website. Viel Spaß beim Backen! Der Teig sollte sich vom Schüsselrand lösen. Beim Mischen mit der Küchenmaschine darauf achten, den Teig nicht zu überkneten. Die ideale Teigtemperatur nach dem Kneten beträgt 28 °C. candidateAudit.text: 💘 Friends? Dates? Flirting? Something in between? Meet queer people in Vienna without swiping. 📅 Sat, 26 September 2026 ⏰ 19:00–21:00 📍 Villa Vida Café, Linke Wienzeile 102, 1060 Vienna 🎟️ €20 per person · cash at the door 💛 Soli tickets available 📝 Registration required 🌈 Who is it for? Queer people who want to meet other queer people — whether you’re looking for dating, friendship, flirting, new connections, or simply meeting more of the community. You’ll meet multiple people through a series of short mini-dates. Privately note who you’d like to connect with again — romantically, platonically, or otherwise. If you both choose each other, it’s a match. 💌 Contact information is only shared with mutual matches. 🧍 Coming alone? Absolutely. You don’t need to know anyone beforehand. The structured format is there to make meeting people easier, including if you’re shy, introverted, or not into approaching strangers at a bar. 💛 Can’t comfortably afford €20? Soli tickets are available. Request one in the comments when registering — no explanation or justification needed. 🤝 Consent, boundaries and mutual respect are essential. A conversation or flirtation never creates an obligation to share contact details or meet again. Discriminatory or harassing behaviour is not welcome. ♿ Step-free access · accessible seating & toilet · service animals welcome. Please note that simultaneous conversations can mean significant background noise. 📝 Register via the link in bio/event page. Come as you are and see who you click with. 💘

The SΫS SPACE prototype by artists duo MUELLER-DIVJAK opens its doors for two afternoons in September, inviting you for a one-of-a-kind experience, an exclusive multisensory trail of resonating with and better understanding of living systems. ⚡⚡⚡Currently all individual time slots are taken, but you can sign up for the waiting list! Find the link in our bio! Exclusive one-hour slot for a fascinating journey into your senses and search for a being that knows and feels everything about connectedness and interdependence. The artist and researcher duo MUELLER-DIVJAK (Dr. Jeanette Müller and Dr. Paul Divjak), who is working at the AIL with international artists and systems scientists on the FWF/PEEK project SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS. Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenographies for Systems Awareness (Project lead: Mag. Alexandra Graupner; University of Applied Arts), is devoted to creating experiential multisensory spaces – the so called SΫS SPACEs – that help enhancing systems awareness through special sensory cues. Such allowing for coping resiliently with the complex interrelations and interactions that shape our world and all our lives. mueller_divjak dieangewandte

candidateAudit.text: Der Kornspitz: Was 1984 in Österreich als kleines resches Weckerl begann, eroberte schon bald Brotkörbe und Frühstückstische weit über die Landesgrenzen hinaus. Wer lernen möchte, wie man den Kornspitz und weitere Gebäcke mit Körnern und Saaten wie ein Profi backt, ist in unserem Kurs „Knuspriger Kornspitz – Backen mit Saaten“ genau richtig! Kurstermine und Buchung findet ihr auf unserer Website: www.krusteundkrume.at Rezept KÖRNERBRÜHSTÜCK 25 g Roggenvollkornmehl 25 g Haferflocken 50 g Sesam 50 g Sonnenblumenkerne 50 g Leinsamen 5 g Brotgewürz 260 g Wasser, kochend HAUPTTEIG abgekühltes Brühstück 30 g Altbrot 190 g Wasser (20 °C) 480 g Weizenmehl 700 20 g Backhefe 20 g Honig 13 g Salz 8 g Roggenmalz 8 g Rapsöl 1. Körnerbrühstück: Alle trockenen Zutaten in eine Schüssel geben und verrühren. Die gleichmäßig vermischte Menge mit dem kochendem Wasser überbrühen, das Brühstück in der Schüssel abgedeckt mind. 3 Stunden abkühlen lassen. 2. Hauptteig: Das Altbrot in der Schüttflüssigkeit für 15 Minuten einweichen, pürieren und mit allen anderen Zutaten in eine Knetschüssel geben. Dann 10 Minuten langsam mischen, das Salz hinzufügen und weitere 2-4 Minuten etwas schneller kneten, bis er eine geschmeidige Oberfläche aufweist und sich vom Schüsselrand löst. Die ideale Teigtemperatur nach dem Mischen beträgt 25-28°C. Den fertigen Teig in einer Schüssel zugedeckt 30 Minuten rasten lassen. 3. candidateAudit.title: The Unsafe+Sounds festival, held annually in Vienna, returns in September with a kaleidoscopic program, offering a multifaceted glimpse into the contemporary music scene and AIL is
candidateAudit.text: The Unsafe+Sounds festival, held annually in Vienna, returns in September with a kaleidoscopic program, offering a multifaceted glimpse into the contemporary music scene and AIL is delighted to once again host one event in the program. unsafeandsounds AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna (Free entry) Overview: 18:30 Panel Discussion, unsafe+sounds in cooperation with the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures (University of Applied Arts Vienna) weibel.institute Affective Histories Timotheus Vermeulen and Christian Höller in conversation with Sophie Publig History is never simply given. It is made through the scales and materials by which the past becomes legible: from sweeping narratives and historical events to gestures, sounds, images, technical infrastructures, and seemingly minor traces SOPHIE PUBLIG is a Senior Scientist researching digital ecosystems. Based at the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, she navigates the intricate networks of online territories. TIMOTHEUS VERMEULEN is Professor of Media, Culture and Society at the University of Oslo and joint director of the Media Aesthetics Research Group. He was a visiting scholar in Art History at Harvard in 2023–24 and will serve as joint Principal Investigator on a project on the politics of tone at the Centre for Advanced Study in Oslo in 2027–28. CHRISTIAN HÖLLER is editor and co-publisher of springerin – Hefte für Gegenwartskunst. Since 2024 he is head of the department Cross Disciplinary Strategies at the University of Applied Arts Vienna. cro

candidateAudit.text: Looking for a relaxed way to spend your Saturday evening? candidateAudit.title: Throughout August and September, the artist duo MUELLER-DIVJAK is residing at AIL for Summer Studio – using the space for artistic research, experimentation, and learning, developi
candidateAudit.text: Throughout August and September, the artist duo MUELLER-DIVJAK is residing at AIL for Summer Studio – using the space for artistic research, experimentation, and learning, developing the project's multisensory scenography – the so-called SΫS SPACE. Aim of the Summer Studio is to prepare the prototype of the scenography, which will be established at the AIL in June 2027 as the centerpiece of the final exhibition of the PEEK project ’SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS — Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenography for Systems Awareness.’ The SΫS SPACE facilitates a physical experience of one's own embededdness within living systems, within complex interrelationships – within a greater whole. It paves the way for relational sensing and thinking – an embodied systems awareness, that can help in coping with complexity, challenges, and uncertainties, and in making good decisions towards sustainable futures. It deliberately reduces the dominance of the sense of sight, placing the emphasis instead on smell, touch, and hearing. Numerous scientists, as well as invited artists, politicians, journalists, children, senior citizens, curators, cultural workers, educators, and teenagers are individually guided through the immersive environment by Jeanette Müller and Paul Divjak and share their responses in photo-based reflections and semi-structured interviews. Their feedback directly informs the prototype. Save the date! 14 and 15 Sep 2026 The SΫS SPACE will open to the public in individual time slots for an exclusive multisensory experience. candidateAudit.text: A LIFE IN LAYERS Art Exhibition at Market Island by Marlis Dsouza artsybym A collection of works from across Marlis Dsouza’s artistic journey, bringing together pieces from ‘NEW Wave’, ‘FEAR-LESS’, The ‘Marlis’ Collection, and ‘One for the Pages’. candidateAudit.text: 🎬 Sapphic Film Series: Rebel Dykes Punk meets feminism at the next edition of our Sapphic Film Series at Villa Vida Café. 🖤 Join us for a free screening of Rebel Dykes, a documentary exploring the lives of a group of lesbians who helped shape a radical queer subculture in 1980s London. Through stories of friendship, sex, activism, nightlife, art and resistance, Rebel Dykes takes us into a world where punk collided with feminism and queer people created their own spaces, communities and ways of living. Rather than presenting queer history as something distant or polished, the documentary is told through the people who were there — the rebels who lived, loved, organised, partied and challenged expectations both inside and outside feminist movements. candidateAudit.text: Every drag performance tells a story. Whether it’s joyful, political, deeply personal, or completely absurd, the most memorable performances come from artists who know how to connect with an audience. Join drag artist DaDa JV for an interactive workshop exploring the art of storytelling through drag and performance. Together, you’ll look at how movement, music, character, costume, emotion, and stage presence work together to create performances that leave a lasting impact. This workshop is open to performers of all experience levels, from those taking their first steps into drag to seasoned artists looking to deepen their creative practice. Participants are encouraged to bring ideas, works in progress, or simply their curiosity. Together we’ll explore: • Finding your unique performance voice • Building a story through movement and music • Connecting authentically with an audience • Using drag as a tool for self expression and community • Developing confidence on stage Expect a welcoming, collaborative environment where experimentation is encouraged and every participant’s perspective is valued. Event Details Saturday, August 29 4:00 PM Villa Vida Café, Linke Wienzeile 102, 1060 Vienna This workshop is donation based. Give what you can. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. Come ready to learn, share, and discover new ways to bring your story to life on stage.

candidateAudit.text: Over the past season, every spin, every step, and every dance has made a real difference. 💜 Thanks to your generosity, Queer Salsa Wien has raised over €850 for the Queer Vienna Mutual Aid Fund (QVMAF) this year already. The Queer Vienna Mutual Aid Fund provides one-off emergency microgrants to queer people in Vienna experiencing unexpected financial hardship. Whether someone is struggling to pay rent, buy groceries, cover medical costs, or get through another crisis, these grants help community members when they need it most. A huge thank you to the incredible Queer Salsa Wien team for organising these classes, and to everyone who has danced, donated, volunteered, and supported this initiative. Every donation, no matter the size, helps build a stronger community based on solidarity and mutual care. Queer Salsa classes will be back at Villa Vida in October but in the meantime you can join their outdoor classes and parties. Follow queersalsawien for information. The Queer Vienna Mutual Aid Fund is an initiative started by hint.wien and villavidacafe. If you’d like to learn more about the Queer Vienna Mutual Aid Fund or make a donation, visit queervienna.at. See you on the dance floor soon. 💃🏽🕺🏿❤️ 💜 Thank you, queersalsawien ! Over €850 raised for the Queer Vienna Mutual Aid Fund in 2026—thank you to everyone who danced and donated. QVMAF provides emergency microgrants to queer people in Vienna facing unexpected financial hardship. Learn more or support the fund at queervienna.at

candidateAudit.title: The exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory is still running till this Friday, July 10! Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Last guided tour: Thur, July 9, 17:00 Memory is not
candidateAudit.text: The exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory is still running till this Friday, July 10! Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Last guided tour: Thur, July 9, 17:00 Memory is not a stable record of the past. Rather than functioning as a static archive, it unfolds as a dynamic process in which traces are continuously reshaped by perception, narration, and material conditions. Across these artistic approaches, [REVERBERATED] invites visitors to consider memory not as something simply preserved, but as something continuously produced through interactions between bodies, technologies, and environments. The exhibition thus explores how the past continues to reverberate within the systems of the present. With contributions by: Agustina Belén Agüero, Lobna Awidat, Phin Anibal, Rimon Alyagon Darr, Ronnie Danaher, Tatiana Del Valle, Hasti Ghasedi, Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz, Hanna Hofmann, Tal Horesh, Mauritius Itzinger, Laura Isselhorst, Dina Karaman, Moritz Klarer, Anna Buchner, Leonard Otterbein, David Ristić, Rajarshi Sarkar, Agnes Schyberg, Aryan Shahabian, Majedeh Shahvelayati, Mehrta Shirzadian, Pauline Simon, Laura Chalabi, People of Soil Photos: Lea Dörl

candidateAudit.text: A new series of postcards is now installed at Café Exchange cafe_exchange The series was extracted from the course ‘Drawing: Here & Now’ by Simon Goritschnig zeichnungunddruckgrafik In collaborative drawing, two people share a single pen – the line becomes a space of negotiation. A play between control and letting go. Who leads – and when? Impulse meets resistance, conviction meets empathy. Not always a conversation, but always an understanding – a dance on paper. These and other experiments are part of the course “Drawing: Here & Now” by Simon Goritschnig, in which students of the department Drawing and Printmaking explore various qualities of drawing beyond observational study. In the project “Reflex,” these experimental setups are set against observational drawing. Students draw in the cashier hall of the former Postsparkasse, intuitively picking up details from architecture and space, as well as situations of coming together: conversations, movements, gazes. In this process, it becomes visible how public and social space is visually probed and explored. The focus lies on reflection — with, through, and within drawing. With contributions by: Andrea Vairelles, Anna Marino, Beth Sorby, Emilia Schönwiese, Flora Schmid, Hannah Horn, Henriette Sonntag, Leo Hasslinger, Maria Lutkova, Max Offergeld, Nikolaus Kohout, Sophie Schweizer, Anija S Dartizio, Timo Pfeifer, Vera Kügel AIL in cooperation with the department Drawing and Printmaking and Simon Goritschnig Image: Henriette Sonntag Design: Atelier Dreibholz Concept Postcard Editions and Production: Eva Weber

candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 4 Jul 2026, 15:00 The Geography of Yellow Walls Performance by Mehrta Shirzadian mehrrta Bright yellow becomes a quiet declaration of care, resistance, and return. Here, the body is reclaimed as homeland, shaped by experience rather than imposed borders. A performance unfolding through turmeric as healing material and the body as living territory. The work is rooted in a deep commitment to women’s health and critical scientific perspectives, engaging forms of embodied knowledge that have long been ignored or erased. The body becomes both evidence and memory, offering its own geography as a space of protection, defiance, and belonging. The performance is adapted to each site, responding to the spatial and contextual conditions of different venues. Mehrta Shirzadian is a performance and multimedia artist and artistic ­researcher working at the intersection of art and science. With a background in molecular biology, mathematics, and computer science, she creates participatory works exploring microbial life, sound, and bodily ecologies, addressing embodiment, agency, and the politics of representation. candidateAudit.text: On view till Saturday (18:00) – An installation presented by the department of Digital Arts / Part of Angewandte Festival René’s Collapse Collection’ is a fictional startup and alternative investment platform that explores the cultural, economic, and emotional afterlife of the collapse of René Benko’s SIGNA empire. Through NFTs, merchandise, video works, and performative sales strategies, the project examines how value is produced through speculation, narrative, and collective belief. Originally developed through public interventions, the project was expanded through a student take over by Digitale Kunst. This exhibition presents new project strands developed by the students: an NFT series reflecting on financial dependency, a merchandise collection appropriating the aesthetics of startup culture and luxury branding, and a series of short-form videos combining influencer culture, promotional performance, and social commentary. Operating at the intersection of installation, performance, and participatory fiction, Renés Collapse Collection invites visitors to engage directly with the mechanisms of speculation, value production, and collapse. candidateAudit.text: In a world that is seemingly always connected, we lose ourselves in constant contact. As part of Angewandte Festival, AIL presents: Sich zusammen schreiben [to get in touch], A performance and poem by Carla Schwering and Timna Lugstein from by the department of Institute of Fine Arts & Media Art – Photography (Sophie Thun) The phrase "Schreiben wir uns zusammen" that on the surface means something like “let’s write to each other again in more detail” actually implies a postponement. In the performance, the artists type excerpts from their shared chat history in a poetic arrangement on two typewriters facing each other – messages in which they attempt to get closer to one another. The time and effort spent cancelling meet ups, for which there is supposedly no capacity is made visible. With the postcards created for the performance, visitors can reconnect with a long-lost friend. On the occasion of Angewandte Festival AIL hosts a selection of performances and installations in the cashier hall and the current exhibition will have more activations. candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 3 Jul 2026, 15:30 Darf ich noch einen Satz? (Palimpsest for 8 speakers) Performance by Leonard Otterbein leonard.ottb The audio performance Darf ich noch einen Satz? (Palimpsest for 8 speakers) explores how sound can model processes of memory formation and transformation. Layered oscillations and brief sound textures repeat with phase shifts, gradually overlapping and partially canceling each other out, much like the traces in an overwritten manuscript. The work is inspired by memory research on reconsolidation – in which recalling an event alters its stored form – and its cultural studies counterpart, reconstructivity. The piece is composed of multiple layers of sound that continuously overlap anew, attempting to cancel each other out in the process. In this process, however, the layers are never completely erased, so that fragments of the preceding states always remain Leonard Otterbein is a sound artist and composer with a background in ecology and ecotoxicology, where he studied mixture effects of agricultural pesticides and nanoparticles. His work spans instrumental and electroacoustic composition, examining perceptual thresholds. He works with psychoacoustic effects and approaches sound as spatial and sculptural material shaped by its relation to space. Part of the exhibition [REVERBERATED]. candidateAudit.text: From the project SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS. Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenography for Systems Awareness – a performance by mueller_divjak in front of Otto Wagner Postsparkasse as part of Angewandte Festival! 'LIMINAL TRACES. Celebrating Acoustic Ecologies' is a dynamic sound lecture that understands the acoustic world as a phenomenon of resonance, shaped by connectedness and interaction. Through the live-curated interplay of field recordings, physical and digital artefacts, the performance traces sonic imprints deeply embedded in our collective memory, presenting them as a new listening experience. Developed within SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS at the AIL, this solar performance explores the intersections of sound, pop history and solar energy, celebrating concept, improvisation and the (unexpected) emergent. The performance ends when the energy collected by the mobile solar unit runs out. — The artist and researcher duo MUELLER-DIVJAK (Dr. Jeanette Müller and Dr. Paul Divjak), who conceived and initiated SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS, is working since 2023 at AIL with international artists and systems scientists to form experiential spaces by artistic means (scenographies) and to create sensory impressions that help us to better understand and resonate with living systems. During the project essential principles of living systems are transformed into olfactory, auditory and tactile artworks / artefacts and used experimentally. Team: Jeanette Müller, Paul Divjak, Alexandra Graupner, Anna-Maria Irgang

candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 3 July 2026, 15:00 Hypervigilant Performance by Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz iukumukui Part of the exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory artscience.ak Constant vigilance can develop as a response to racial discrimination and transgenerational trauma, allowing potential threats to be recognized in advance. This fight-or-flight state activates the nervous system and can lead to chronic muscle tension and bruxism. Teeth grinding occurs as a way of coping with stress during sleep, often driven by societal expectations to suppress fear or anger. Hypervigilant addresses this suppressed anger. Aluminum teeth suspended from the ceiling form a space similar to a cage that oscillates between protection and exposure. Shaped as gong-like instruments, the oversized representation of the artist’s bite is set into vibration during a sound performance to release embodied pressure and reduce tension in the nervous system. Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz’s practice centers on suppressed experiences expressed in imagined worlds. Through performative sculptures and installations, she examines spatial dynamics and power structures. Addressing socio-political themes such as racism, sexism, gender, and sexuality, she builds subconscious environments using reference-based objects and constructions in combination with text and sound. candidateAudit.text: As part of Angewandte Festival, AIL presents: Performance by Laura Oyuela and Ádám Salomvári (students of the department Cross-Disciplinary Strategies) Rocks, I mean; - Stars is a sonic and spatial performance departing from text, soundscapes, spoken words and its physical surrounding. The piece works with analogies between black holes and human beings through low frequencies, orbital motion, and stretched time, shaping a field that gathers bodies into one another. The project investigates how perceptual, cognitive, and affective dynamics shape the experience of artistic performance in relation to contemporary conditions of subjectivity, particularly isolation and hyperproductivity. The performance is part of the Cross-Disciplinary Strategies Master’s program exhibition 2026. The work is realised with the technical support of ÆSR Lab, which has contributed to its sonic and spatial development. Photo: earthboundeva

candidateAudit.text: This is Bome. A collective hub. Not just a coffee shop. Not just a toast atelier. The name comes from our mother tongue, Kurdish. Bome means crazy like us, like our whole team.
